data.narrative:
Claros is a Seed-stage climate and energy company founded by Daniel Kultran and Grant Verstandig that has raised $30M to date. The broader Climate & Energy sector comprises one public comparable (LNZA) and eight private peers including Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, Electric Hydrogen, and Enovix.

The valuation analysis relies primarily on stage-progression methodology, as peer-median comparison is not applicable. The Climate & Energy peer universe, while containing eight same-sector companies, lacks sufficient narrow-filter datapoints at the same stage or adjacent stages to support a robust peer median. Accordingly, stage-progression anchors to the $30M total raised as a proxy for current value, applying a 2.5x multiplier typical of Seed-to-next-stage progression, yielding $75M implied valuation.

This single-method triangulation supports a valuation range of $64M (low) to $86M (high), centered at $75M median. The primary uncertainty stems from limited comparability within the narrowly-defined Climate & Energy frontier-tech space at early stages; a median derived from the broader eight-peer set would carry lower conviction. Valuation sensitivity remains elevated to near-term financing activity and sector-wide funding conditions, which have historically driven significant variance in early-stage climate-tech pricing.
